facts.fact: Internet Society Pulse, from PeeringDB data of August 2026, shows SIXP Sudan (Sudan Internet Exchange Point) with four members at 1 Gbps each, three using RPKI, and no ASN joined or left in the previous 12 months; city not given.
Internet Society Pulse lists two PCH autonomous systems (AS3856 and AS42), registered in the United States, among the four members of SIXP Sudan in August 2026, alongside Sudatel and Zain.

PeeringDB's record for SIXP Sudan (Sudan Internet Exchange Point), operated by the National Information Center of Sudan in Khartoum, shows 4 peers, 4G total capacity and 50% IPv6, last updated 2020-01-22.

note: Minister discussed strengthening internet exchange points with AFRINIC and ISOC at WSIS 2026; no exchange named, nothing in service or planned stated.

facts.fact: The National Information Center's WSIS Forum 2016 deck lists a National Internet Exchange Point among its services, saying it keeps traffic within Sudan, keeps service available nationally during an internet blackout and lowers internet costs; no members or city given; the deck carries no date, so the published date is used.

note: Starlink availability article; Sudan appears only as a date-unspecified market, and the exchange points named (NAPAfrica, JINX, KIXP, IXPN Lagos) are in other countries.
